newsitem.title: USA: Penn Traffic to pare employees, reduce costs.
newsitem.headline: Penn Traffic to pare employees, reduce costs.

text.p: Supermarket operator Penn Traffic Co. said Tuesday first quarter 1997 revenues fell 8.3 percent from a year earlier and it was reorganizing its management in a move to save the company $12 million a year.

It plans to centralize management in its Syracuse headquarters and remove layers of management throughout the organisation. The management reorganization will result in the layoff of approximately 325 nonstore employees, with most of the layoffs coming in the Columbus, Ohio, and DuBois, Pa., divisional headquarters.
The Company said it expects the reorganization will reduce operating costs by approximately $12 million a year.

"These cost-savings will benefit investors, customers and employees," said Phillip E. Hawkins, president and chief executive officer of Penn Traffic, which operates 265 supermarkets in upstate New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania and West Virginia.
The company said sales for the quarter were $759 million, down 8.3 percent from the same period last year. Sales for stores open at least a year were down 8.1 percent.

Penn Traffic will record a pre-tax charge of about $11 million in the first quarter and a pre-tax charge of about $2 million in the second quarter related to the management reorganization and related corporate actions.
In addition, Penn Traffic will record a pre-tax charge of approximately $4 million in the first quarter in connection with the retention of recently hired corporate executives.
The company said it will report full financial results for the quarter on June 2.
The company said its "disappointing" sales reflect the continuation of a recent trend and the impact of newly implemented grocery merchandising programmes.
In the 1996 first quarter, Penn Traffic had a net loss of $9 million, or 83 cents a share, on revenues of $827.7 million.
Penn Traffic stock was down 50 cents at $6 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
